# mirtverse

**From item responses to defensible decisions, with or without writing R
code.**

*Türkçe:* [mirtverse’e Türkçe
giriş](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/tr.html) ve [Türkçe
özet kılavuz
(PDF)](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/cheatsheet/mirtverse-cheatsheet-tr.pdf).

**mirtverse** is a friendly workflow and reporting layer for the
[mirt](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/) package by R. Philip
Chalmers. mirt estimates item response theory (IRT) models; mirtverse
helps you choose a model, understand the results, make publication-ready
figures, and share everything with people who never open R.

![The mirtverse workflow in four steps: Bring your data, fit and choose
a model, understand the results, share and
decide](reference/figures/home-workflow.svg)

[![Four mirtverse outputs: A results dashboard, an item health card, a
Wright map and a DIF
plot](reference/figures/home-showcase.png)](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/gallery.html)

**Try it without installing anything:** [Open the live example
dashboard](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/dashboard/sat12-demo.html)
or browse the
[Gallery](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/gallery.html) of
figures and outputs.

**Or watch a short demo** (about 90 seconds each, with captions):

[![Video: A tour of the point-and-click
workbench](reference/figures/home-video-workbench.png)](https://youtu.be/huSxZzaFNs0)
[![Video: The AI Hub, with automated scoring checked like a
psychometrician
would](reference/figures/home-video-ai-hub.png)](https://youtu.be/4cFjnpSkcMQ)
[![Video: The thesis kit, from a fitted model to an APA Methods
paragraph](reference/figures/home-video-thesis-kit.png)](https://youtu.be/J3us00sk34g)

## Find your way in

| I am… | Start here |
|----|----|
| A student learning IRT or analysing thesis data | [Students](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-students.html) · [Thesis kit](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/thesis-kit.html) |
| An instructor teaching measurement (book, ten labs, sample syllabus) | [Instructors](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-instructors.html) · [Adopt for your course](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/adopt.html) |
| A psychometrician at a testing or credentialing program | [Testing programs](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-practitioners.html) · [Case study](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/case-study.html) |
| A researcher who already uses mirt, ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ | [Researchers](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-researchers.html) · [Moving to mirt](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtify.html) |
| New to R, or coming from Winsteps, SPSS or Excel | [New to R](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-new-to-r.html) |
| Curious about AI in measurement | [AI Hub](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/ai-hub.html): Book chapters, labs and a workshop kit |

Not sure which IRT model fits your data? The [Which IRT model?
flowchart](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/which-model.html)
goes from what one item score looks like to a model and the line of R
code that fits it ([printable
poster](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/which-model/which-irt-model.pdf)).

[![Animated: Item text and responses flow through a neural network and
come out as a calibrated item characteristic
curve](reference/figures/home-ai.svg)](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/ai-hub.html)

## Get started

``` r

install.packages("mirtverse", repos = c("https://okanbulut.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
# Development version: remotes::install_github("okanbulut/mirtverse")

library(mirtverse)

data <- expand.table(LSAT7)

sel <- select_model(data)   # compares Rasch, 2PL and 3PL and recommends one
mod <- sel$best             # an ordinary mirt model

interpret(mod)              # what the results mean, in plain language
item_table(mod)             # item statistics, fit and flags in one table
gg_wright(mod)              # person-item map
item_card(mod, "Item.2")    # one-page item review

mv_report(sel, file = "report.html")        # everything in one HTML file
mv_dashboard(mod, title = "LSAT results")   # interactive dashboard to share
```

Prefer clicking? Run
[`launch_workbench()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md),
which writes the R code for you. Every function is listed in the
[Reference](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/), and the
[cheat sheet
(PDF)](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/cheatsheet/mirtverse-cheatsheet.pdf)
groups them by task.

## Beyond the usual IRT toolkit

- **Describe the analysis, get the script.**
  `mv_ask("fit a 2PL, check DIF by gender and make a report", data = mydata)`
  writes a tested R script from one sentence, with Claude, an OpenAI
  model, a local model or an offline parser. [How it
  works](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mv-ask-guide.html)
- **Let Claude run the analysis.** The mirtverse plugin for Claude Code
  turns Claude into a psychometrician that fits models, checks items and
  DIF, scores people, explains the results and leaves a report and an R
  script, all with mirtverse on your own computer:
  `/plugin marketplace add okanbulut/mirtverse`, then
  `/plugin install mirtverse@mirtverse`. [The mirtverse
  agent](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtverse-agent.html)
- **Generate items.**
  [`generate_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  drafts multiple-choice items with keys and open-ended items with
  rubrics from a test blueprint, and
  [`generate_isomorphs()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_isomorphs.md)
  builds item families from an item model. [Book
  chapter](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/book/aig.html)
- **Score open-ended responses.**
  [`train_scorer()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/train_scorer.md)
  trains a transparent scoring engine that runs offline, and
  [`score_open()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/score_open.md)
  scores with it or with a language model, checking agreement with human
  raters before any score is used. [Book
  chapter](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/book/auto-scoring.html)
- **Run a whole testing program.**
  [`mv_pipeline()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_pipeline.md)
  takes a test from blueprint to bank monitoring in 13 stages, with
  flags that catch problems before the next step. [The
  pipeline](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/assessment-pipeline.html)
  · [Case
  study](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/case-study.html)

## About mirt

[mirt](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/), developed and maintained
by [Dr. R. Philip Chalmers](https://chalmers.info.yorku.ca/), is one of
the most comprehensive open-source packages for item response theory. It
estimates unidimensional and multidimensional models with more than 30
item types, multiple-group and mixed-effects models, and latent class
and diagnostic models, with EM and MHRM estimation, fit statistics, DIF
and ability estimation.

**mirtverse depends on mirt and never changes how models are
estimated.** Every function accepts a model created with
[`mirt::mirt()`](https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/reference/mirt.html),
so you can move between the two packages at any point.

## Citation

Please cite mirtverse together with mirt. Run `citation("mirtverse")` in
R, or use:

Bulut, O. (2026). *mirtverse: Accessible, AI-ready item response theory
in R with mirt* \[Preprint\]. PsyArXiv.
<https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/j9ya7_v1>

Bulut, O. (2026). *mirtverse: A friendly workflow and reporting layer
for ‘mirt’* (Version 0.5.0) \[R package\]. Zenodo.
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23719384>

Chalmers, R. P. (2012). mirt: A multidimensional item response theory
package for the R environment. *Journal of Statistical Software, 48*(6),
1-29. <https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v048.i06>

The preprint describes the design of mirtverse and its AI layer; the
software citation records the version you used. To cite all versions of
the software, use <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23719384>, which
always resolves to the latest release. The online book has its own DOI:
[10.5281/zenodo.23885605](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23885605).

# Package index

## Workbench

Point-and-click analysis with reproducible code.

- [`launch_workbench()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md)
  [`workbench_app()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/launch_workbench.md)
  : Launch the mirtverse workbench

## Scripts from plain language

Describe an analysis in words and get a complete, tested R script.

- [`mv_ask()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_ask.md)
  : Write an analysis script from a plain-language request
- [`mv_ask_setup()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_ask_setup.md)
  : Set up an AI model for mv_ask()
- [`mv_plan()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_plan.md)
  [`update_plan()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_plan.md)
  : An analysis plan for mv_ask()
- [`run_script()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_script.md)
  [`save_script()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/run_script.md)
  : Run or save a script written by mv_ask()
- [`profile_data()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/profile_data.md)
  : Summarise a data set without revealing its values

## Coming from other IRT packages

Translate ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ code into mirt code.

- [`mirtify()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify.md)
  : Translate ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ code into mirt code
- [`mirtify_crosswalk()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mirtify_crosswalk.md)
  : The ltm, eRm, TAM and irtQ to mirt crosswalk

## Assessment pipeline

Take a test from response data to a technical report in stages, with
checks and flags to consider before each next stage.

- [`mv_pipeline()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_pipeline.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_pipeline>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_pipeline.md)
  : Start an assessment pipeline
- [`set_blueprint()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/set_blueprint.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Test blueprint and construct definition
- [`generate_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  [`add_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  [`verify_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_items.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Item generation
- [`review_packet()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/review_packet.md)
  [`read_reviews()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/review_packet.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Item review
- [`design_field_test()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/design_field_test.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Field-test design
- [`add_responses()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/add_responses.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Data intake and cleaning
- [`calibrate()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/calibrate.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Calibration
- [`link_to_bank()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/link_to_bank.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Link a calibration to an item bank
- [`bank_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/bank_items.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Add items to a bank
- [`mv_bank()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_bank.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_bank>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_bank.md)
  : An item bank
- [`assemble_forms()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/assemble_forms.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Assemble fixed test forms
- [`simulate_cat()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/simulate_cat.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Simulate a computerized adaptive test
- [`assemble_mst()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/assemble_mst.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Assemble and simulate a multistage test
- [`set_cuts()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/set_cuts.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Cut scores and decision quality
- [`item_map()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_map.md)
  : Item map for Bookmark standard setting
- [`score_open()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/score_open.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Scoring open-ended responses
- [`score_persons()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/score_persons.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Score test takers
- [`check_security()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/check_security.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Test security
- [`pipeline_report()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/pipeline_report.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Technical report
- [`monitor_bank()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/monitor_bank.md)
  : Pipeline stage: Bank monitoring
- [`retire_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/retire_items.md)
  : Retire bank items or send them back to review
- [`flags()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/flags.md) :
  List the flags raised by a pipeline
- [`acknowledge()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/acknowledge.md)
  [`override()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/acknowledge.md)
  : Record a decision about a flag
- [`drop_items()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/drop_items.md)
  : Remove items from a pipeline
- [`mv_rules()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_rules.md)
  : Thresholds for the pipeline checks

## AI in measurement

Run the language model features offline from recorded responses,
describe items by their text and predict their difficulty, generate
items from item models and calibrate their families, train and check an
automated scoring engine, audit AI components and draft a validity
argument, simulate respondents with a language model (experimental),
check where synthetic respondents land in the real population, and
teaching datasets with item text, written answers, a field test of
generated items, an AI-scored test and HEXACO answers of real people and
four language models.

- [`mv_llm_replay()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_llm_replay.md)
  [`mv_llm_record()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_llm_replay.md)
  [`mv_llm_recordings()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_llm_replay.md)
  : Replay or record language model responses
- [`item_features()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_features.md)
  : Text features of test items
- [`predict_difficulty()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/predict_difficulty.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_difficulty>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/predict_difficulty.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<mv_difficulty>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/predict_difficulty.md)
  [`predict(`*`<mv_difficulty>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/predict_difficulty.md)
  : Predict item difficulty from item features
- [`item_model()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/item_model.md)
  : Write an item model for automatic item generation
- [`generate_isomorphs()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/generate_isomorphs.md)
  : Generate isomorphs from item models
- [`calibrate_families()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/calibrate_families.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<mv_families>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/calibrate_families.md)
  : Calibrate item families
- [`train_scorer()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/train_scorer.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_scorer>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/train_scorer.md)
  : Train an automated scorer on human-scored text
- [`predict(`*`<mv_scorer>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/predict.mv_scorer.md)
  : Score new responses with a trained scorer
- [`agreement_report()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/agreement_report.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<mv_agreement>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/agreement_report.md)
  : Agreement between machine and human scores
- [`rater_facets()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/rater_facets.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_facets>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/rater_facets.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<mv_facets>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/rater_facets.md)
  : Place human and AI raters on the Wright map
- [`scoring_shift()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/scoring_shift.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_shift>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/scoring_shift.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<mv_shift>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/scoring_shift.md)
  : Compare item thresholds and scores under human and AI scoring
- [`ai_audit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/ai_audit.md)
  [`tidy(`*`<mv_audit>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/ai_audit.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<mv_audit>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/ai_audit.md)
  : Audit an AI component before its results are used
- [`validity_argument()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/validity_argument.md)
  [`format(`*`<mv_validity>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/validity_argument.md)
  : Draft a validity argument for an AI component
- [`simulate_llm_respondents()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/simulate_llm_respondents.md)
  : Simulate respondents with a language model (experimental)
- [`compare_synthetic()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/compare_synthetic.md)
  : Compare simulated respondents with real ones (experimental)
- [`synthetic_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/synthetic_coverage.md)
  : How well do synthetic respondents cover the real population?
- [`blend_llms()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/blend_llms.md)

  : HEXACO responses of real people, for checking synthetic respondents
- [`hexaco_llm`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/hexaco_llm.md)
  : HEXACO responses generated by four language models
- [`hexaco_items`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/hexaco_items.md)
  : The 240 IPIP-HEXACO items and their keys
- [`itemtext`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/itemtext.md)
  : Numeracy items with their text, for the AI Hub
- [`essays`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/essays.md) :
  Short science explanations scored by raters, for the AI Hub
- [`aigfield`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/aigfield.md)
  : A field test of generated mathematics items, for the AI Hub
- [`aigfield_items`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/aigfield_items.md)
  : The generated items of the AIG field test
- [`aiscored`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/aiscored.md)
  : An AI-scored science test over two years, for the AI Hub
- [`aiscored_cr`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/aiscored_cr.md)
  : Machine and human scores of the AI-scored test

## Knowledge graphs

Describe what a test measures as a graph of concepts, their
prerequisites and the items that measure them; check the graph for
problems and draw it; turn it into a Q-matrix, a confirmatory mirt model
or the mastery patterns its prerequisites allow; check it against data
and apply the changes the data suggest; explain item difficulty with it,
using item metadata too; draft a graph from item text with a language
model (experimental). Examples with a simulated fractions test (with the
true graph) and Tatsuoka’s fraction subtraction data.

- [`mv_kg_build()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_build.md)
  : Build a knowledge graph of concepts and items
- [`as_mv_kg()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/as_mv_kg.md)
  : Turn other objects into a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_check()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_check.md)
  : Check a knowledge graph for problems
- [`tidy(`*`<mv_kg>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg.md)
  [`glance(`*`<mv_kg>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg.md)
  : Tidy and glance methods for knowledge graphs
- [`gg_kg()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_kg.md) :
  Draw a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_qmatrix()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_qmatrix.md)
  : Q-matrix from a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_model()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_model.md)
  : Write a mirt model from a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_irt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_irt.md)
  : Fit a confirmatory IRT model built from a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_hierarchy()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_hierarchy.md)
  : Mastery patterns allowed by the prerequisites
- [`mv_kg_fit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_fit.md)
  : Check a knowledge graph against response data
- [`tidy(`*`<mv_kg_fit>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_fit.md)
  [`glance(`*`<mv_kg_fit>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_fit.md)
  : Tidy and glance methods for knowledge graph checks
- [`mv_kg_refine()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_refine.md)
  : Apply suggested changes to a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_edit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_edit.md)
  : Add or drop edges of a knowledge graph by hand
- [`gg_kg_fit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_kg_fit.md)
  : Draw the data's evidence on a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_explain()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_explain.md)
  : Explain item difficulty with a knowledge graph
- [`tidy(`*`<mv_kg_explain>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_explain.md)
  [`glance(`*`<mv_kg_explain>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_explain.md)
  : Tidy and glance methods for explained item difficulty
- [`mv_kg_subset()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_subset.md)
  : Keep part of a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_annotate()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_annotate.md)
  : Add item metadata to a knowledge graph
- [`mv_kg_extract()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_extract.md)
  : Draft a knowledge graph from item text with a language model
- [`tidy(`*`<mv_kg_draft>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_draft.md)
  : Tidy methods for drafted knowledge graphs
- [`mv_kg_compare()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/mv_kg_compare.md)
  : Compare a knowledge graph with a reference graph
- [`tidy(`*`<mv_kg_compare>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_compare.md)
  [`glance(`*`<mv_kg_compare>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/tidy_mv_kg_compare.md)
  : Tidy and glance methods for graph comparisons
- [`fractions`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/fractions.md)
  [`fractions_kg`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/fractions.md)
  : Grade 5 fractions test with its knowledge graph
- [`fraction_subtraction`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/fraction_subtraction.md)
  [`fraction_subtraction_kg`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/fraction_subtraction.md)
  : Tatsuoka's fraction subtraction data with its Q-matrix

## Choosing and understanding a model

  : Model selection assistant

  : Plain-language interpretation of IRT results
- [`interpret_prompt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/interpret_prompt.md)
  : Build a prompt for an AI assistant from a fitted model

  : Write the Methods paragraph for an IRT analysis

  : Tidy item statistics and item fit in one table

## Graphics

- [`gg_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_coverage.md)
  : Draw the coverage strip
- [`gg_dif()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_dif.md)
  : DIF effect sizes plot
- [`gg_empirical()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_empirical.md)

- [`gg_info()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_info.md)
  : Test and item information curves
- [`gg_itemfit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_itemfit.md)
  : Item fit plot
- [`gg_kg()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_kg.md) :
  Draw a knowledge graph
- [`gg_kg_fit()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_kg_fit.md)
  : Draw the data's evidence on a knowledge graph
- [`gg_q3()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_q3.md) :
  Local dependence heatmap (Yen's Q3)
- [`gg_scores()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_scores.md)
  : Distribution of person scores
- [`gg_trace()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_trace.md)
  : Item characteristic (trace) curves
- [`gg_wright()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/gg_wright.md)
  : Wright map (person-item map)
- [`autoplot(`*`<SingleGroupClass>`*`)`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/autoplot.SingleGroupClass.md)
  : Plot a mirt model with ggplot2
- [`theme_mirtverse()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/theme_mirtverse.md)
  : A clean ggplot2 theme for psychometric graphics

## Instructor toolkit

Build labs on your own data, adapt the built-in labs and the book’s
chapters, swap datasets and check materials before class.

- [`new_course()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/new_course.md)
  [`course_materials()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/new_course.md)
  : Start a course folder for the instructor toolkit
- [`new_lab()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/new_lab.md)
  : Build a lab from your own data
- [`copy_lab()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/copy_lab.md)
  : Copy a built-in lab into a course to edit it
- [`lab_section_types()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/lab_section_types.md)
  : Sections you can add to a toolkit lab

  [`add_lab_exercise()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/add_lab_section.md)
  [`add_lab_question()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/add_lab_section.md)
  [`remove_lab_section()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/add_lab_section.md)
  [`lab_outline()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/add_lab_section.md)
  : Add, remove and list the sections of a lab
- [`swap_lab_data()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/swap_lab_data.md)
  : Replace the data in a toolkit lab
- [`lab_data()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/lab_data.md)
  : Load the data of a toolkit lab
- [`copy_chapter()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/copy_chapter.md)
  [`new_chapter()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/copy_chapter.md)
  [`swap_chapter_data()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/copy_chapter.md)
  [`book_chapters()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/copy_chapter.md)
  : Notes chapters for a course
- [`copy_workshop()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/copy_workshop.md)
  : Copy the AI in measurement workshop kit
- [`check_material()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/check_material.md)
  : Check a lab, a chapter or a whole course
- [`preview_lab()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/reference/preview_lab.md)
  : Open a lab in the browser

# Articles

### Start here

A short path for each kind of user.

- [Start here:
  Students](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-students.md):

  A path for graduate students: Fit, check and explain an IRT model for
  a course or thesis, with figures a committee will accept.

- [Start here:
  Instructors](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-instructors.md):

  A complete IRT course in a box: A free book, ten interactive labs, a
  course map, and tools to adapt everything to your own data.

- [Start here: Testing
  programs](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-practitioners.md):

  For psychometricians at testing organizations and credentialing
  bodies: Run a program from blueprint to bank monitoring, with every
  decision flagged, reviewed and documented.

- [Start here:
  Researchers](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-researchers.md):

  All of mirt, with tidy outputs, ggplot2 figures and one-call reports,
  so analyses are reproducible and figures are publication-ready.

- [Start here: New to
  R](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/for-new-to-r.md):

  Get IRT results without learning R first: Point and click in the
  workbench, describe the analysis in words, or share a dashboard.

- [mirtverse: Türkçe
  tanıtım](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/tr.md):

  mirtverse paketinin Türkçe tanıtımı: Paketin ne yaptığı, kurulumu, ilk
  analiz ve Türkçe özet kılavuz.

### Guides

- [Tutorial: A first analysis with
  mirtverse](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtverse.md):

- [The mirtverse
  workbench](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/workbench.md):

- [Which IRT model? A one-page
  flowchart](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/which-model.md):

  A decision flowchart that goes from what one item score looks like to
  an IRT model and the line of R code that fits it, with a printable
  poster and a worked example for every path.

- [Response times and rapid
  guessing](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/response-times.md):

- [mv_ask(): From a sentence to a tested R
  script](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mv-ask-guide.md):

  How mv_ask() turns a plain-language request into a complete IRT
  analysis script, with worked examples and benchmark results for
  Claude, GPT and local Ollama models.

- [The mirtverse agent for
  Claude](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtverse-agent.md):

  Install the mirtverse plugin for Claude Code and let Claude analyze
  your test data with item response theory: Model choice, item checks,
  DIF, scores, plots, a report and a reproducible R script.

- [Sharing results with a
  dashboard](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/dashboards.md):

  Turn a fitted model into an interactive dashboard for people who do
  not use R, and share it as a single HTML file or a Shiny app.

- [Moving from ltm, eRm, TAM or irtQ to
  mirt](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/mirtify.md):

  Translate existing IRT code into mirt with mirtify(), see what changes
  and why, and look up any function in the crosswalk.

- [An assessment pipeline from blueprint to bank
  monitoring](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/assessment-pipeline.md):

  Take a certification exam through every stage of the mirtverse
  assessment pipeline, with the checks and decisions at each step.

- [Case study: A certification exam, from field test to
  pass/fail](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/case-study.md):

  A fictional certification board takes a 32-item exam through the
  mirtverse assessment pipeline. Eight decisions, each recorded, and a
  technical report to download.

- [Thesis kit: From item responses to a Methods
  section](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/thesis-kit.md):

  A step-by-step path for a thesis or dissertation that uses IRT: Check
  the data, choose and check a model, make the figures, and draft the
  Methods paragraph with cite_methods().

- [Gallery](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/gallery.md):

  Every figure and output mirtverse makes, with the code for each one.

- [Video demos](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/videos.md):

  Short narrated demos of mirtverse: The point-and-click workbench, the
  AI Hub and the thesis kit, about 90 seconds each with English
  captions.

### Teaching and learning

- [Adopt mirtverse for your
  course](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/adopt.md):

  Everything an instructor needs to teach item response theory with
  mirtverse: A sample syllabus to edit, a free book, ten labs, and a way
  to hear about updates.

- [Teaching labs for measurement
  courses](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/teaching-labs.md):

  Interactive learnr labs in which students fit live mirt models and
  make the decisions a psychometrician makes, from scoring and model
  choice to interpretation and fairness. Includes an instructor guide
  and answer key.

- [A course map for
  instructors](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/course-map.md):

  A suggested 12-week syllabus for a university course in item response
  theory, linking each week to mirtverse articles, labs, functions and
  datasets.

- [The instructor
  toolkit](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/instructor-toolkit.md):

  Build interactive labs on your own data, adapt the built-in labs and
  the book’s chapters, add exercises and questions, swap datasets, and
  check everything before class.

- [An AI assistant for your course
  materials](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/instructor-mcp.md):

  Connect Claude or an OpenAI assistant to your mirtverse course folder
  and revise labs, chapters and notes, or bring your existing materials
  into mirtverse, by describing what you want.

- [Glossary of IRT
  terms](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/glossary.md):

  Plain-language definitions of the terms used in item response theory,
  each with the mirtverse or mirt function that computes it, and
  pictures where a picture helps.

### AI in measurement

Artificial intelligence and machine learning for psychometricians. These
articles are also in the AI Hub menu.

- [AI Hub: Artificial intelligence for
  psychometricians](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/ai-hub.md):

  Start here to learn how artificial intelligence and machine learning
  fit into psychometrics and educational measurement: A learning path,
  what mirtverse can already do with AI, and where to read more.

- [Checking synthetic respondents: The coverage
  strip](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/synthetic-coverage.md):

  How to see where respondents generated by a language model land in the
  real population, how to read Overlap and Structure, and how to compare
  models, groups and items, with HEXACO answers from four language
  models and 17,874 real people.

- [Machine learning for psychometricians: A translation
  table](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/ai-translation.md):

  More than 40 machine learning and AI terms, each with what it means,
  the psychometric idea closest to it, and where the two part ways.

- [AI in measurement: A reading
  list](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/ai-reading.md):

  An annotated list of books, papers and guidelines on artificial
  intelligence in psychometrics and educational measurement, grouped by
  topic, for psychometricians who are new to the area.

- [AI in measurement: A one-day
  workshop](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/ai-workshop.md):

  A ready-made kit for a one-day workshop on AI in measurement: Slides,
  a facilitator’s guide and four offline labs, for psychometricians and
  testing-program staff.
